chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halby, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one who did not catch the sermon on Friday. He said: 'He prays two rak'at. And if the prayer missed him and he did not catch it, let him pray four.'
And he said: 'When you catch the Imam before he bows in the last rak'at, you have caught the prayer. And if you caught him after he had bowed, it is Zuhr, four (rak'at).'

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ: To catch or join in time
key_terms.الْخُطْبَة: The sermon delivered before the Friday prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who joins Friday prayer late or misses it entirely?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential principle that catching the Imam's bowing (ruku') in the final rak'ah is the decisive criterion for valid Friday prayer participation. It distinguishes between the obligation of the two-rak'ah Friday prayer and the four-rak'ah Zuhr prayer based on the precise moment of joining the congregation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the congregational aspect of Friday worship. This ruling ensures that latecomers are not penalized for minor delays while maintaining the integrity of the communal prayer structure.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the ones did not achieve the sermon on the day of Friday. Heasws said: ‘He should pray two Rak’at. But, if he misses the Salāt and does not achieve it, so let him pray four (Rak’at)’.

And heasws said: ‘When you achieve (being with) the prayer leader before he performs Rukū in the last Rak’at, so you have achieved the Salāt, and even if you achieve it after him having performed Rukū, so it is Al-Zohr of four (Rak’at)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from af-Halabiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who misses to attend the sermon of Friday. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can perform the two Rak‘at, but if he misses Salah (prayer), he performs four Rak‘at.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If you join the Imam before the Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) for the last Rak‘at, you have attended Salah (prayer), but if you join the Imam after Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) of the last Rak‘at, then it is al-Dhuhr and four Rak‘at.’”
